name: cellcell-compete-div
description: M7b dividing-population competition: two DIVIDING founder LINEAGES race for one glucose pool supplied at a fixed level from the boundary (Dirichlet BC value 8.0, chemostat-like), each cell growing by per-cell dFBA and DIVIDING at a volume threshold into a lineage (CpmCompeteDivision, a CpmGrowthDivision subclass), with a maintenance cost (0.10/tick) and a viability floor (biomass < 1.25 -> the cell is removed from the lattice via the native remove_cells -- a genuine death, not just displacement). Founder 1 is the FAST lineage (glucose_vmax 10, left) and founder 2 the SLOW lineage (glucose_vmax 4, right) -- the same 10-vs-4 uptake asymmetry as cellcell-compete, now heritable through division. MEASURED OUTCOME (M7b, tests/test_cellcell_m7.py): robust population-level COMPETITIVE DOMINANCE of the fast lineage -- by t=40 the fast lineage holds ~9x the slow lineage's biomass (seed 1: fast 122 in 48 cells vs slow 13 in 5 cells) across all seeds tested. This is competition-driven, not intrinsic non-viability: the slow lineage SURVIVES in monoculture under the identical supply/maintenance/floor (~22-33 cells; see the cellcell-compete-div-slowmono control) but is suppressed to a few cells when the fast lineage preempts the shared glucose (Tilman R*: the faster competitor draws glucose below the slow lineage's break-even). FULL competitive exclusion (slow lineage driven to zero) occurs at the deterministic headline seed by t~56 and in 2/5 seeds of a robustness sweep, but is NOT the robust outcome -- in the other seeds the suppressed slow lineage persists in spatial refugia near the supplied boundary. So the earned term is competitive DOMINANCE / suppression; strict exclusion is stochastic here, not deterministic.
